caption_latex: \textbf{Observed-test placement gains need not survive autonomous feedback.} Training effects subtract base-only error from mixed-training error under the same policy; all lower policy rows show this effect. Risk gaps subtract random-placement error from risk-placement error; their change compares the training arms. Dots show paired seeds; diamonds and bars show mean $\pm$ sample seed SD, not confidence intervals. Each panel has its own scale. In Goop, one mixed-training seed-2 trajectory hit the candidate-pair limit under each of native, dense and cached-risk evaluation. These training effects and the change in risk gap have no three-seed mean; the completed seed-0 and seed-1 points remain visible. WaterDrop RMS was not evaluated because it was not included in that study. Observed risk scores the preceding observed base graph; autonomous risk caches its own preceding graph.
